Verasight owns verified humans but sells sample, so opposing counsel would call it conflicted. Pew and NORC publish the methodology for free but not per case, and not in expert-report form. Panel-owner stacks (Kantar Qubed, Research Defender, PureScore, Pori) are the self-grading problem that Daubert challenges target. Existing litigation-survey consultancies field surveys and testify on merits, so they are customers, not rivals.

mutants.title: Contingency Recovery for Contaminated Survey Sample
mutants.one_liner: A freight-audit-style recovery firm that finds contaminated and duplicated completes in the survey sample buyers already paid for, files credit claims against panel vendors, and keeps 25-35% of what it recovers.
mutants.customer: Wedge: mid-size full-service market research agencies (about 100-500 staff) that buy $1-10M a year of third-party online sample on fixed-fee client projects and absorb the reruns. Second wave: procurement teams at CPG, pharma and financial-services firms that already run recovery audits on freight, telecom and cloud spend but have never applied one to research sample.
mutants.problem: The parent idea asks insights teams to pay for a quality audit, and the research found no evidence anyone will pay $3-15k for one. Buyers do pay for money back. Kantar says post-field reconciliation (rejected sample) rates are up about 300% in three years, with some clients rejecting up to 40% of data (a vendor source). Contaminated completes that pass screening are paid for and used. The same panelist or device is also resold through several exchanges, so buyers pay twice for one human. Agencies eat the rerun cost, procurement never sees data quality, and nobody has respondent-level evidence strong enough to make a vendor pay. Vendors also fight individual rejections because their detector disagrees with the buyer's.
mutants.solution: Zero-upfront retrospective audit. The buyer gives read access to 12-24 months of respondent-level files, vendor IDs, invoices and MSAs. The firm runs LLM-assisted open-end forensics, cross-vendor duplicate detection (hashed device, IP and open-end similarity) and paradata review. It ingests detection flags from dtect, Verisoul or DQC where the buyer already has them. A 300-500-complete verified-human control cell per major vendor calibrates a population-level contamination estimate with error bounds. The firm then files claims for replacement completes, credits or refunds, citing the contractual quality clause. Claims argue that a vendor's batch exceeded the SLA (e.g. above 5% invalid, 95% CI) rather than fighting each flagged complete, which is where vendors dispute. Fee is 25-35% of value recovered, with no recovery meaning no fee. Stage two is prospective: a payment-hold or escrow layer where vendor payment for a batch releases after a control-calibrated pass, and a monitoring subscription.
mutants.why_now: Agents passing attention checks mean the largest share of contamination is now undetected at entry, which is exactly the paid-for-but-invalid pool that recovery targets. The cost stack collapsed: reading 10 million open-ended answers used to need human coders at dollars per complete, and LLMs now do it at fractions of a cent, so a contingency model works even on mid-size invoices. Pew's Aug 2026 study and NORC's fraud review give claim letters a public, credible methodology to cite. Buyers are already 'auditing suppliers, bringing sampling in-house and demanding accountability' (Greenbook), so procurement is primed.
mutants.revenue_model: Contingency fee of 25-35% of recovered value. Illustrative unit economics, which are assumptions to test: $3M annual sample spend, 5-10% recoverable ($150-300k), 50% recovered, 30% fee, so $22-45k per customer per year. That is lower than the parent's $50-150k programmes but has almost no sales friction. Add-ons are a prospective monitoring subscription ($2-4k/month) and escrow at 1-2% of sample spend. Roughly 150-250 agencies and 30-60 enterprise buyers as a bottom-up serviceable market gives a $10M+ ARR business without ever selling 'quality' as a line item.
mutants.non_obvious_insight: Nobody budgets for data quality, but everyone has a process for accounts receivable. Turning 'is my sample clean?' into 'how much money are we owed?' moves the buyer from the insights head, who has no budget and no pain, to finance and procurement, who have both. The scarce asset is the same verified-human reference as in the parent, but used differently. It is needed only in small doses (a few hundred humans per vendor), which removes the 2,000-person panel problem and lets it be licensed instead of built. Population-level SLA claims also sidestep the detector-disagreement fight that makes per-complete rejections so contentious.
mutants.first_30_days: Days 1-7: post to insights and procurement communities and DM 20 agency founders and heads of ops. The offer is 'send one vendor's last quarter of respondent files, we tell you the recoverable amount, you pay nothing unless we recover'. Days 5-15: have a contract lawyer review 10 sample sample-vendor MSAs and SOWs to extract quality, replacement and dispute clauses, and draft a standard claim letter. Days 10-25: build the pipeline (open-end similarity, hashed-device dedupe across vendors, control-cell comparison) and buy 300 completes each from 4 major vendors as baseline. Days 20-30: sign 3 contingency agreements and file the first claim. Success is the first $50k recovered by day 90. Kill if, after 5 audits, recoverable value is below 2% of spend or vendors refuse every claim.
mutants.how_it_avoids_competitors: Detection and scorecard vendors sell information or prevention: Verisoul, dtect, Roundtable, CloudResearch Sentry, ReDem and CleanID filter at entry, and DQC sells supplier benchmarks and a trust score. None recovers money already paid, and all are cheap enough to be input suppliers rather than rivals. Panel-owner stacks (Kantar Qubed, Research Defender, PureScore, Pori) are the counterparty being claimed against, not a competitor. Verasight sells sample and could not credibly run claims against other vendors. The firm takes no referral fees from any vendor and never sells sample, so it stays neutral. Pew and NORC publish methodology free but never file claims. Traditional recovery-audit firms (freight, telecom, healthcare billing) do not touch survey sample, and the defensibility comes from the vendor-by-vendor claim-outcome database, which sets settlement rates and improves each claim.

mutants.title: Independent Answer Key for Synthetic Respondents
mutants.one_liner: Invert the referee: a neutral scoring authority that holds fresh, verified-human ground truth, and scores synthetic-respondent and digital-twin vendors against it in quarterly pre-registered, sealed-prediction benchmarks.
mutants.customer: Two-sided. Vendors: synthetic-respondent, persona and digital-twin startups and the survey platforms adding synthetic boosts. Buyers: CPG, pharma and financial-services insights and innovation teams and research agencies being pitched 'AI respondents' and unsure whom to believe. Later: AI labs that need uncontaminated human-opinion evals.
mutants.problem: Synthetic-respondent vendors claim high accuracy on self-chosen benchmarks. Backtests against old polls leak, because published polls and concept-test norms are in the models' training data, and vendors can cherry-pick questions. Buyers have no neutral way to tell which claim is real before betting a launch decision on it. The parent evidence that agents pass 99.8% of attention checks shows LLM personas mimic humans on surface features, which cuts both ways: it enables fraud and it makes synthetic research plausible. Nobody holds fresh verified-human answers on questions asked after model cutoffs, with the vendor's predictions locked in beforehand.
mutants.solution: A predict-then-reveal benchmark. Each quarter, the firm and a buyer advisory board write about 80 novel questions and concepts, including anonymised buyer concept tests under NDA. Vendors submit hash-committed sealed predictions of the answer distributions for named demographic targets. The firm fields the items to 1,000-3,000 verified humans, address-recruited and device-attested, licensed from partners (NORC, Verasight, Prolific or a university survey centre) so no one panel controls the answer key. It scores distribution error, rank-order of concept winners, subgroup fidelity and calibration of stated uncertainty, and publishes a leaderboard. Vendors pay for private diagnostics and for a licence to cite their scored accuracy, never for placement. Buyers pay for full reports and for a 'bake-off as a service', running a shortlist of 3 vendors on 10 of the buyer's own concepts against 400 verified humans. Endgame: the growing library of pre-registered human ground truth becomes shared infrastructure. It calibrates hybrid human-plus-synthetic samples, is licensed to AI labs as fresh opinion evals, and feeds the original bot-audit business off the same panel.
mutants.why_now: Synthetic-respondent and digital-twin companies raised large rounds in 2025-26 and are getting enterprise pilots (specific rounds not verified in this session, so check). Model releases every few months make static benchmarks stale and leaky, which turns a benchmark into a recurring re-fielding business. Pew's Aug 2026 study is a public design template for benchmarking against address-recruited samples. Buyers who lived through the panel-fraud scare now ask 'how do you know it is right?' by reflex.
mutants.revenue_model: Vendors pay $8-25k per quarterly private diagnostic and $30-100k/yr for an audited accuracy-claim licence. Buyers pay $10-25k/yr for full reports and $20-40k per bake-off. Founding-member pre-sales fund wave 1: 8 buyers at $15k covers a 1,000-human wave. Later, AI-lab dataset licences of $100-500k/yr. Control-panel cost is the main COGS at about $10-40 per verified complete, which suggests 60-70% gross margin once pre-sales cover each wave.
mutants.non_obvious_insight: The verified-human panel is worth more as the answer key for AI than as a shield against AI, and the business wins whichever way the synthetic-research bet goes. If synthetic respondents work, everyone needs a scorer and a calibration anchor. If they fail, buyers need proof and a return to human samples. Fraud and progress both raise demand for the reference. The product is not data but a commitment protocol (sealed predictions, then reveal), which solves the training-data leakage that no static dataset can. Refusing to be scored becomes a signal of weakness, which is the flywheel that turns a benchmark into a standard, the way MLPerf-style or leaderboard-style evaluators gained authority.
mutants.first_30_days: Days 1-10: write the protocol and scoring spec (sealing method, metrics, no pay-for-placement rule) and publish it openly. Recruit 5 founding buyer-side advisors (CPG or pharma insights heads) at $5k pilot memberships. Days 5-20: invite 6-8 synthetic-respondent vendors to a free founding wave slot in exchange for submitting sealed predictions. Days 15-30: finalize 40 novel questions, hash-commit vendor predictions, and field wave 0 to 600-1,000 verified humans from a partner for roughly $10-20k. Publish the first leaderboard by day 45. Kill test: fewer than 4 vendors willing to submit, or fewer than 3 buyers who say they would pay for the results.
mutants.how_it_avoids_competitors: Every competitor in the parent's research defends human samples against bots (Verisoul, dtect, Roundtable, CloudResearch, Kantar Qubed, PureScore, ReDem) or sells verified sample (Verasight), or writes standards without testing (GDQ). None scores synthetic respondents. CloudResearch's Bot Olympics grades detectors on its own turf and is not neutral. Verasight's replication of Pew shows its own panel is cleaner, so it sells sample and could not be an arbiter between vendors that compete with its product. DQC is neutral but aggregates fraud signals. It does not run sealed-prediction tests against fresh human truth. Pew and NORC could field this, but a non-profit research org will not run a recurring commercial scoring service. Academic synthetic-survey benchmarks exist but are static and leak into training data. I could not verify whether a commercial neutral scorer already exists because the web-search budget ran out, so check before building.
